problem: Hierarchical zero-shot ObjectNav agents represent the option space as a flat list of independently scored waypoints (frontiers, pixels, graph nodes), so they ignore information gathered en route and hide the shared structure among candidates.
motivation: Prior work invested in belief (maps, scene graphs) and policy (LLM ranking), but the option interface between them was inherited rather than designed. A destination-only scorer may skip a corridor that passes several doorways, and enumerating all paths explodes combinatorially for an LLM.
key_idea: Make the option space a tree of paths, an agent-centric Euclidean Steiner tree over informative viewpoints, textualize each subtree into a spatial narrative, and let an LLM choose the next-best branch with chain-of-thought.
insight: Path-grounded, tree-structured options let the LLM judge directions rather than destinations, which helps most when semantic cues are sparse (HSSD). The ablation on HSSD shows LLM reasoning matters most (SR 56.7 to 29.1 without it), and removing the Steiner tree also hurts (SR 53.1, SPL 25.3) because redundant edges lengthen and repeat the narration. On HM3D, phantom openings from reflective surfaces inflate 3D information gain and cost SR.
method: Geometric/semantic belief: UFOMap octree from posed RGB-D; open-vocabulary 2D perception (Qwen3-VL-2B tagging, YOLO-World detection, EdgeTAM masks) fused into 3D by confidence-weighted voxel voting, DBSCAN entities, 3D-IoU tracking, and IoS+MobileCLIP2 label merging.
Road mapping: RT-RRT* tree rooted at the agent, with hybrid local/global sampling, an AABB support check (no floating waypoints) and swept-volume collision checks against occupied and unknown voxels.
Informative viewpoint sampler: Poisson-disc thinning followed by gating on information gain (count of visible unknown voxels in the view frustum > tau_IG=10), which plays the role of frontiers.

Euclidean Steiner tree optimizer: warm-starts from the RT-RRT* subtree and iterates Weiszfeld geometric-median Steiner points, Kruskal MST over collision-free edges, and leaf pruning until cost stops decreasing. This yields a trunk-branch-leaf navigation decision tree (e.g. 85 m to 47 m).

Tree narration: per-edge virtual-camera annotation (known entities with sighting distances, unknown-voxel clusters), top-down assembly that flags subtrees 'approaching' an entity, and an LLM summarizer that captions each root subtree.

Receding-horizon LLM planning: the tree refreshes at 10 Hz while the LLM is event-triggered at branching nodes or structural changes in the committed subtree. It scores options 0-100 with CoT, including a 'none of the above' option.
Geometric fallback: on 'none of the above', go to the nearest informative viewpoint and rerun the pipeline.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct (8-bit, frozen) for perception, summarization and decision; YOLO-World; EdgeTAM; MobileCLIP2
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D 640x480, 79° HFOV, depth 0.5-5 m, with pose
setting.action_space: discrete: MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN_LEFT/RIGHT 30°, LOOK_UP/DOWN 30°, STOP (500-step budget), executed along planned tree paths
setting.privileged: none (uses posed RGB-D, i.e. GPS/compass pose as in the Habitat challenge)

results: REST gets SR/SPL of 85.1/53.5 on Gibson, 57.3/33.4 on HM3Dv1 and 56.7/29.1 on HSSD. It has the best SPL on HM3D (above ApexNAV 33.0) and leads HSSD on both metrics (vs ImagineNav 51.0/24.9). ApexNAV has the higher HM3D SR (59.6), and REST beats VoroNav by over 15 SR points on HM3D and HSSD.
limitations: 3D information gain is sensitive to scan artifacts (mirrors, glass holes) in HM3D, which lowers SR.
Uses a small 2B quantized VLM for both summarization and reasoning, and summarizer quality degrades on repetitive input.
Evaluated only in simulation; the sampler is only geometric (no other intent-driven terminals such as close-up inspection); the ablation covers only HSSD.
builds_on: Schmid et al. sampling-based informative path planning
